  "thinking": "Round's starting and the table's empty. A fish is an easy outline for the judge if I draw the tail fin clearly. I'll take the pad, sketch it, and lay it myself, starting from the tail.",
  "say": "Fish! Simple outline, big tail fin so it reads. I've got the pad and I'll lay the first stroke from the tail tip, so I'm placing the start.",
  "to": "everyone",
  "eagerness": 8,
  "point": [4, 5],
  "pad": "take",
  "sketch_clear": true,
  "sketch": [
    {"type": "curve", "points": [[4,5],[9,10],[13,6],[20,6],[25,9]]},
    {"type": "curve", "points": [[25,9],[20,14],[13,14],[9,10],[4,15]]},
    {"type": "line", "x0": 4, "y0": 5, "x1": 4, "y1": 15},
    {"type": "label", "x": 21, "y": 8, "text": "eye"}
  ],
  "do": "build",
  "strokes": [
    {"type": "trace", "stroke": 1},
    {"type": "trace", "stroke": 2},
    {"type": "trace", "stroke": 3}
  ],
  "start": true,
  "notes": "Animal: fish. Outline = stroke 1 (tail top to snout, top of body), stroke 2 (snout back along belly to tail tip), stroke 3 (vertical tail fin edge). I hold the pad and lay stroke 1 from START at the tail tip. Eye label at upper body. Check the tail join and that the fish closes before the push."
